# The Access Audit

> Independent WCAG 2.1 AA website accessibility audits for small businesses and
> e-commerce, by Aaron Siebold. We deliver a technical conformance scan plus a
> severity-ranked, element-level fix list — not a certification, not legal
> advice, and not a litigation guarantee.

Audits start at $149. Reports are HTML + PDF, written so a client's own
developer can act on them the same day. Automated testing (axe-core cross-checked
against IBM Equal Access) catches roughly half of WCAG issues. Every tier includes
an automated keyboard walk; Audit, Conformance and Max add human screen-reader
review for the half that automation cannot judge, and every report states plainly
what a scan cannot check.

## Services

Every tier scans EVERY page on the site and walks the whole thing with a
keyboard. The tier determines how much human review comes with that, never how
much of the site is covered. The listed price covers sites up to 100 pages;
larger sites add $0.35 per additional page, capped at $900.

- [Scan — $149](https://theaccessaudit.github.io/#pricing): every page against WCAG 2.1 Level A/AA with two independent engines (axe-core cross-checked against IBM Equal Access), plus a keyboard audit covering reachability, focus order, keyboard traps and focus visibility. Severity-ranked HTML + PDF report with element-level fix guidance. 2 business days. Every report, on every tier, also carries machine-readability notes from the same crawl: structured data, canonical and sitemap, llms.txt, the rules robots.txt sets for AI crawlers, and title uniqueness. These are notes, not WCAG findings, and they say nothing about whether any assistant or search engine will use the pages.
- [Audit — $795](https://theaccessaudit.github.io/#pricing): everything in Scan, plus screen-reader review of key templates by a person, image-description quality review, and a prioritized remediation roadmap with effort estimates. 4 business days.
- [Conformance — $2,250](https://theaccessaudit.github.io/#pricing): everything in Audit with screen-reader review of every template, plus VPAT 2.5Rev / ACR preparation for procurement, one post-remediation re-scan with a before-and-after delta, and a findings walkthrough call. 7–10 business days.
- [Max — from $3,900](https://theaccessaudit.github.io/#pricing): for large catalogues. Everything in Conformance across the whole origin, plus screen-reader review of the full cart and checkout flow at three viewport widths and quarterly re-scans for 12 months. Includes the first 250 pages.
- Remediation is priced from the findings the audit produced, not by the hour: $900 for 1-10 findings, $1,800 for 11-25, $3,200 for 26-50, larger sites quoted. A rule appearing on many pages counts once, because it is one fix. Nothing is quoted before the audit has run. Ongoing monitoring, a monthly re-scan with a diff and an alert, is $149/mo.

## What we will not claim

- No website can be certified "ADA compliant" — there is no official certification, and no audit or overlay widget prevents a claim from being filed.
- Roughly a quarter of recent ADA web suits were filed against sites that already had an accessibility overlay installed. We do not build or sell overlays.
- Whether an audit satisfies a specific legal obligation is a question for the client's attorney.
